- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent reversal, but true outcome shows mean reversion, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture momentum shifts; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 5% from model’s final 10-day average, reweight final 30d forecast toward recent 10d data (especially if sentiment is volatile).
